sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and purpose
sections.what: Loads the environment report and the live check functions. The header explains that it runs without a server and never shows secret values.
sections.why: Keeps the check standalone so it works when the server will not start.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Main check
sections.what: Prints the settings and warnings, runs the test on the fallback model and each role, prints each verdict, then exits with a pass or fail code.
sections.why: Likely reason: one command gives a full picture of the AI setup.
sections.watch_out: Each run makes real model calls, so it can be slow or cost a little when the network is down.

summary: Command line check that the AI model gateway works. It prints the settings, sends a tiny test request to the main model and each role, and reports pass or fail.
purpose: Lets the owner test the AI connection without starting the server or logging in.
why: Likely reason: a quick way to diagnose AI failures from the command line.
how: Builds an environment report showing the models, gateway and any missing critical settings, and prints warnings. Sends a five token test to the fallback model and then to each role. Exits with 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail, and 2 if the script crashes.
inputs: Environment settings read by the environment report. No command line options.
outputs: A printed report and an exit code.
risks: Each check is a real model call, so it costs a little and depends on the network. Must never print secret values, and the header says it prints only presence and length.
debug: Read the verdict line. It distinguishes gateway authentication, provider key and model not found problems. Check the environment report for missing critical settings.
